Your workbench is a tool, your most important one. Best way to get a good one is to not buy a premade one from Home Depot/Lowes. Gert on craigslist and search "workbench" and see if you can find one in the size you want. An all metal frame & legs is easier to transport and set-up than an all wood one. Ideally the one you find has a butcher block top. If it doesn't but as good legs and frame get back on craigslist and search "butcher block". Small kitchen or parson's tables are the right size for a workbench and the tops are easy to pull off. If you don't find an actual workbench and don't mind sitting you can use the table as is. If you can't find any of the above a steel desk is a great work area (again you must sit at it) but there is a lot of storage for tools. Next you need a good 4" vise that is bolted to your work top. Look for an old Craftsman or any US, Japan, or Euro made one. The cast-iron is usually ductile iron and way more resistant to cracking than cheap import vises. Finally, good lighting over your work area is critical. Natural white LED or halogen will show colors in their most natural way. Getting hand tools are fine but you absolutely must have a proper place to use them.

My favorite and most amazing prize possession is a belt driven mini table saw built in America in the 80's. Every part of it is replaceable, you can buy them used for very cheap and they never die. The new Craftsman tools are not made here but the older ones were and they never die so you can find them used very easily.
